- Related to https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/7023.

Note that unlike what https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/7023 proposes, this is not a "transparent" approach to caching. While it avoids incurring a loading time penalty for cold loads (when loading a project for the first time), it does mean you'll have to commit a large binary file to version control, which bloats VCS history. This binary file also has to be included in the PCK file, making it larger in the process. It's also a destructive approach if you don't keep a copy of the original NoiseTexture around – there's no way to edit the original noise once it's converted to a texture.

I still think a caching approach is worth the added complexity, so that users benefit from faster loading times without having to deal about the rest (larger file sizes, destructive workflow). If we want to avoid issues with cold loads, this could even be integrated into a process performed on export like https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/102552 does for shaders.

PS: I suggest saving to lossless WebP if the image size is lower than or equal to 16383 pixels on both dimensions, as lossless WebP is smaller than PNG in terms of file size. It also loads just as fast, if not faster.

@Calinou Thanks, I had a look for existing proposals but somehow didn't find that one, that's helpful context! 

In my use cases the size of the generated file didn't really come up as an issue as it's just one extra resource among many others. I can see how caching would be preferable if that is a problem though.

To address the destructive nature I could add an option in the dialog to preserve the original resource, even though all its uses will be replaced. This would be a difference in behavior from the other plugins though which is maybe not desirable. 

Switching to WebP seems like it makes sense based on what you said, I'll look into that.

I also see I've missed some documentation, I'll address that too.

I think this PR is great. At least for those who need it, they don't have to use scripts for conversion.
 
I found a issue that conversion will crash if NoiseTexture is pink placeholder (noise is null).

This can implements conversion for GradientTexture. In addition, for usability, when the parent directory doesn't exist, it should automatically create it. And when the target path already exists, it should allow to overwrite it.

It is worth mentioning that there is a better and simple way to automatically bake all the noise textures during export and remain editable in editor. https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/7023#issuecomment-2817433102
